Developers environmental advice on planning proposals
Planning Inspectorate Advice Note Seven EIA

official_measurement_examples.name: Schedule 1 rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: Under the planning EIA regime, Schedule 1 development requires EIA; that requirement is procedural and is not itself a decision to grant or refuse planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Schedule 2 screening
official_measurement_examples.fact: Schedule 2 development requires screening for likely significant environmental effects; being within Schedule 2 does not automatically mean an Environmental Statement is required in every case.

official_measurement_examples.name: Screening opinion limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A screening opinion or direction decides whether EIA is required and does not grant planning permission or determine the final planning balance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Scoping opinion limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A scoping opinion defines the expected scope and level of detail for an Environmental Statement; it is not project approval and does not certify every environmental impact as acceptable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Environmental Statement role
official_measurement_examples.fact: An Environmental Statement supplies assessment evidence for EIA development; submission of an ES does not by itself satisfy separate permits, licences, HRA duties or planning conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 PINS currentity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate Advice Note Seven was updated 2 June 2026, while town-and-country-planning EIA remains governed by the 2017 Regulations; current guidance and governing regime must remain distinct.

official_measurement_examples.name: Agriculture EIA separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's agriculture EIA screening and consent process is a separate statutory regime from town-and-country planning EIA and must not be used as a planning-permission proxy.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: EIA status does not determine title, exact buildable area, development yield, infrastructure capacity or final permission outcome for a parcel.

core_rules: Schedule1 EIA requirement is not planning permission
Schedule2 category is not automatic EIA requirement
scoping opinion is not project approval
Environmental Statement is evidence not consent
EIA does not replace environmental permits
agriculture EIA and planning EIA remain distinct
guidance update date is not legislation commencement date
EIA status does not establish ownership
EIA status does not calculate development yield
no parcel EIA clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Planning Inspectorate, Natural England, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. June-July 2026 guidance/register currentity retained with regime, screening, scoping and consent separation; no parcel promotion.
